verdict.rationale: Vercel's docs show on-demand server-side code via Vercel Functions on Fluid compute, git-push deploys of Next.js and 40+ frameworks, container-image functions, WebSockets, and documented limits. Backing data stores are attached via the Marketplace "without managing database servers". A community comment corroborates the smooth "code and go" serverless onboarding; a separate complaint about limited languages is partly answered by the documented container runtime. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement that functions need no server management (the docs say this only for databases), and detailed independent hands-on reports of deploying full-stack apps.

support.subject: As a developer, I can deploy serverless functions and full-stack apps with no servers to manage

citations.quote: Run server-side code on demand with Fluid compute, which scales concurrency for AI and I/O-heavy workloads.
Deploy Next.js with zero configuration, or bring one of 40+ supported frameworks.
Run any code and library on Vercel Functions with an OCI container image built from a Dockerfile or Containerfile at the project root.
connect external Postgres databases to your Vercel projects without managing database servers
